overview: Pleural effusion is the abnormal accumulation of excess fluid in the pleural space between the visceral pleura (lining the lung) and parietal pleura (lining the chest wall). Fluid buildup compresses the adjacent lung parenchyma, hindering normal expansion.
radiographic_findings: Blunting of the posterior (on lateral view, requires ~50 mL) and lateral costophrenic angles (requires ~175-200 mL)
Meniscus sign: upward curved fluid contour along the lateral chest wall
Opacification of the hemithorax with mediastinal shift away from the effusion in large tension effusions
Layering of free-flowing fluid along the dependent chest wall on lateral decubitus radiograph
common_symptoms: Progressive shortness of breath, aggravated when recumbent
Pleuritic chest pain (sharp discomfort during deep inspiration)
Dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds over the affected lung base
Fever or systemic constitutional symptoms when associated with infection (empyema/parapneumonic)
causes_and_risk_factors: Transudative: Congestive heart failure, liver cirrhosis (hepatic hydrothorax), nephrotic syndrome, hypoalbuminemia
Exudative: Bacterial pneumonia (parapneumonic effusion), malignancy (lung, breast, lymphoma), pulmonary embolism, tuberculosis, rheumatoid arthritis, pancreatitis
diagnostic_information: Diagnostic Thoracentesis with pleural fluid analysis
Light's Criteria to differentiate transudate from exudate (fluid/serum protein and LDH ratios)
Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) of the pleural cavity (high sensitivity for fluid quantification)
Pleural fluid cytology and microbiological cultures
treatment_approaches: Therapeutic thoracentesis for immediate symptomatic dyspnea relief
Treatment of underlying etiology (diuretics for CHF; antibiotics for parapneumonic effusion; targeted oncology therapy)
Chest tube thoracostomy (tube drainage) for large complicated effusions or frank pus (empyema)
Chemical pleurodesis or indwelling pleural catheter (IPC) for recurrent malignant effusions
when_to_seek_care: Sudden exacerbation of breathlessness or feeling unable to catch breath
High fever accompanied by purulent sputum or severe localized chest pain
Signs of respiratory exhaustion or hemodynamic instability
